chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is permissible for a man from the wealth of his son? He said: 'His food, without extravagance, if he is in need of it.'

He said: So I said to him, what about the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to the man who came to him and presented his father, saying: 'You and your wealth are for your father'?

He said: 'He only brought his father to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him: O Messenger of Allah, this is my father; my inheritance from my mother has been wronged by him. So the father informed him that he had spent it on himself and on him. So he said: 'You and your wealth are for your father'.
And the man did not have any wealth, so was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) holding the father back from the son?'
ai.seo_question: What is a father's right to his son's wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a father may take from his son's wealth for sustenance without extravagance when in need, reconciling this with the hadith 'You and your wealth are for your father' by explaining that the latter referred to a specific case where the son's inheritance was already being consumed by the father, rather than establishing a general rule of total transfer. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that the father's right is one of necessity and maintenance, not absolute ownership, preserving the son's financial independence. The context underscores the practical application of familial financial duties in early Islamic society, where paternal authority was balanced against the son's right to retain his own assets.
